reproduction_target: Training and evaluation of VariantFormer, a 1.2B-parameter hierarchical transformer predicting tissue-specific gene expression from personalized diploid genomes. Computational scope = the entire study: cohort WGS/RNA-seq acquisition and harmonization (MAGE/1000G, ENTEx, GTEx v9/v10, ADNI, six ENCODE cancer cell lines), personalized-sequence construction via bcftools consensus with IUPAC heterozygote encoding, BPE tokenizer training, mutation-aware encoder pretraining on ENTEx chromatin activity, two-stage expression-model training, and post-training tasks (baseline comparison vs Enformer/Borzoi/EVO 2/genotype-RF, Alzheimer's case-control classification, MAGMA v1.10 gene enrichment, eQTL Catalogue variant-effect benchmarking, in-silico APOE mutagenesis, DNase-seq attention validation). No wet-lab experiments were performed by the authors; all cohorts are pre-existing. |W| = 0.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation derived from Methods sections 5.1-5.4 and 6.1-6.4 of the JATS full text, plus the repo LANDING page and README PROSE (github.com/czi-ai/variantformer). No workflow file (Snakefile/Nextflow/CWL/WDL) is described in prose, so the granularity anchor is the named-tool rule. Reference-genome/annotation setup is kept as its own step because it is pinned to specific assembly and GENCODE releases that every downstream step consumes. The two supervised-training stages are kept separate because they use different gene sets, epoch counts and learning rates. Baseline model runs (Enformer, Borzoi, EVO 2, genotype-RF) are folded into the single expression-evaluation step C20. Supplementary Methods S1.2-S1.6 are referenced by the paper but were not fetched at stage 1; several version/parameter judgements below may move once those are read. NOTE: this is a prose-only pass. The repository tree listing shows a Dockerfile, install.sh, pyproject.toml, configs/*.yaml, tests/ and inference notebooks, but NO source file was read line-by-line and no lockfile presence was confirmed - that is stage-2 work.

steps.label: Reference genome and annotation setup: GRCh38 (GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set_GCA_000001405.15), GENCODE v24 basic annotation (gencode.v24.basic.annotation.gtf.gz), autosomes chr1-chr22 only

Candidate cis-regulatory element acquisition: ENCODE Registry of cCREs (ENCSR487PRC), primary file ENCFF234XEZ.bed.gz, plus donor/tissue-specific ENTEx cCRE annotations (accessions in Supplementary Table 2); n = 1,063,878 cCREs

MAGE / 1000 Genomes high-coverage (30x) WGS download: phased SNV/INDEL/SV panel, 20220422 release (1kGP_high_coverage_Illumina.chrN.filtered.SNV_INDEL_SV_phased_panel.vcf.gz, chr1-22) for 731 samples from ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk
ENTEx phased WGS VCF download from ENCODE (Illumina NextSeq 500); file accessions listed in Supplementary Table 3
GTEx v9 WGS acquisition for 953 individuals from dbGaP (phs000424.v9, genotype dataset phg001796.v1.GTEx_v9_WGS_953.genotype-calls-vcf.c1)
ADNI WGS acquisition (808 participants, LONI Image and Data Archive) and hg19 -> GRCh38 liftover with CrossMap using the hg19ToHg38 chain file

ENCODE cancer cell-line variant calling (A549, GM23248, HepG2, K562, NCI-H460, Panc1): dual-caller DeepVariant v1.6.0 (germline) + DeepSomatic v1.6.0 (tumor-only), somatic-priority merge at overlapping positions, PASS-only filtering, custom INFO origin annotation (details in Supplementary S1.4)
VCF filtering and standardization: restrict variants to cCRE regions and gene transcriptional windows, add 'chr' prefix, reheader against GRCh38, sort, index (bcftools; no version stated)

Personalized diploid sequence generation: samtools faidx extraction + bcftools consensus -H I (IUPAC heterozygote encoding, VariantFormer) and -H A (alt-allele, Enformer/Borzoi/EVO 2); SV/complex rearrangements excluded; cCREs padded 50 bp each side; windows 98 kb (Enformer/Borzoi) and 8 kb (EVO 2) around gene start; genotype baselines use 150 kb windows, MAF > 0.01, biallelic SNPs, mean imputation

Genetic ancestry inference for GTEx and ADNI: PLINK v1.90b6.24 LD pruning (50 SNP window, 5 SNP step, r2 = 0.2), PCA on 20 PCs, KNN classifier (k = 7, distance-weighted Euclidean) trained on 731 1000 Genomes reference samples (AFR/EUR/EAS/SAS/AMR)

MAGE RNA-seq processing: pseudo-counts from Zenodo record 10535719, conversion to TPM using effective gene lengths, read-depth normalization, GENCODE v38 -> v24 identifier mapping via stable Ensembl IDs
GTEx v10 expression processing: GTEx_Analysis_v10_RNASeQCv2.4.2_gene_tpm.gct from the GTEx Portal, RIN > 6 sample filter, standardization to GENCODE v24

ADNI microarray processing (Affymetrix Human Genome U219, 650 participants with paired WGS): RIN > 6 filter, multi-symbol probe splitting, removal of probes below global median intensity, median collapse across probes per gene, quantile normalization, log transform, GENCODE v24 mapping

ENCODE cell-line RNA-seq quantification retrieval: total RNA-seq gene TSVs with GENCODE v24 / GRCh38 - K562 ENCFF171FQU, HepG2 ENCFF863QWG, GM23248 ENCFF640FPG, A549 ENCFF244DNJ, NCI-H460 ENCFF876SRX, Panc1 ENCFF710IFD

Cross-cohort expression integration into a single AnnData object: gene filter (< 20 non-zero counts across samples removed), non-coding tissue-specific 10th-percentile non-zero threshold filter, non-zero-only training values

BPE DNA tokenizer training on reference cCRE sequences (ENCFF234XEZ, +/-50 bp flanks): HuggingFace Tokenizers BPE model, vocabulary size 500, uppercase normalization, IUPAC code filtering (A,C,G,T,R,Y,S,W,K,M,B,D,H,V)

Mutation-aware sequence encoder pretraining on ENTEx chromatin-activity classification: 12-layer transformer encoder, 512-dim token embeddings, ALiBi positional encoding, Flash Attention, forward+reverse strand, tissue-specific classification heads; DDP over 8 GPUs, per-device batch 32, gradient accumulation 12 (effective 3,072), 29 epochs, Adam lr 1e-4, ReduceLROnPlateau (patience 2, factor 0.1), bfloat16 mixed precision

Expression-model training Stage 1 (protein-coding): 18,439 genes, 12 epochs, CRE encoder frozen, gene encoder fine-tuned, modulators trained end-to-end; 376 GPUs x 2 pairs x 2 tissues x 11 accumulation steps (effective batch 16,544), AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0.01, gradient clipping 1.0, warmup-cosine schedule with 1% warmup, bfloat16
Expression-model training Stage 2 (all annotated genes): +32,517 non-coding genes (50,956 total), 10 additional epochs initialized from Stage 1, learning rate reduced to 4e-5 with minimum 1e-6

Gene-expression prediction benchmark: gene correlation and subject correlation on held-out donors, comparing VariantFormer against Enformer, Borzoi, EVO 2 and a genotype random-forest baseline (AlphaGenome explicitly not benchmarked - not released for fine-tuning)

Alzheimer's case-control classification from gene embeddings: random forests per gene (baselines) or per gene-tissue pair (VariantFormer), grid search over n_trees {100,500,1000} and max_depth {10,20,30}, stratified 10-fold CV on training donors, refit on all training donors, OOD test set of 40 held-out subjects (330 subjects total: 215 AD / 155 CN, 16,510 protein-coding genes), training-only top-K selection, nested bootstrap 95% percentile intervals

MAGMA v1.10 gene-based enrichment: PGC Alzheimer's GWAS summary statistics (23andMe excluded), liftover to GRCh38, duplicate-SNP removal (first occurrence retained), 1000 Genomes Phase 3 EUR LD reference, SNP-to-gene annotation with 100 kb upstream / 50 kb downstream windows over GENCODE v24 boundaries

eQTL Catalogue curation and variant-effect benchmarking: six ge datasets (TwinsUK adipose/blood/skin; Braineac2 and BrainSeq substantia nigra / BA9 frontal cortex / putamen), tissue-label harmonization to GTEx nomenclature, LCL removed, SNPs only, top 50,000 pairs per tissue by p-value, MAF < 0.05 subset (top 10,000), ancestry-stratified BrainSeq sets (AF_EUR > 0.10 & AF_AFR < 0.05; AF_AFR > 0.10 & AF_EUR < 0.05), context-window filtering against VariantFormer/Borzoi/AlphaGenome

In-silico APOE mutagenesis on ADNI OOD carriers: rs429358 (chr19:44908684 T>C) and rs7412 (chr19:44908822 C>T) extraction, generation of actual-genotype vs reference-reverted personalized sequences (eps4 N = 12, eps2 N = 1), tissue-conditioned risk-probability comparison (log OR with 95% CI)

Cross-attention vs chromatin-accessibility validation: ENCODE adrenal-gland DNase-seq bigWig (ENCFF632QUC, UBERON:0002369) compared against attention weights for a random subset of 50 protein-coding genes, GENCODE v24 gene starts/strands

headline.static_readiness: 0/25 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 18/25 (72%) steps reach RI at stage-1 prose level; 7/25 cap at NI. The NI steps all fail on the version axis with no software named or no version stated: CrossMap liftover (C6), bcftools VCF standardization (C8), samtools/bcftools personalized-sequence construction (C9), ADNI microarray normalization with no software named (C13), AnnData integration (C15), the baseline benchmark whose Enformer/Borzoi/EVO 2 checkpoints and versions are unpinned (C20), and the DNase-seq attention validation whose 50-gene random subset has no seed or deposited gene list (C25). Data is never the binding constraint: GTEx (dbGaP phs000424.v9) and ADNI (LONI) are controlled-access with documented DAC paths and are therefore scored 2 with the controlled-access flag, and all other sources are public with pinned accessions. The binding constraints are (a) unversioned command-line genomics tooling in the preprocessing chain and (b) the absence, at prose level, of any located training or preprocessing entrypoint - the public repo landing page shows inference notebooks, model modules, configs, tests, an install.sh and a Dockerfile, but no training driver. Under stage-1 rules version is capped at 1 regardless of the Dockerfile, so this bound is a floor: a stage-2 code read could raise version to 2 for the repo-covered steps if the container/lock provides genuine environment closure.
headline.coverage: 25 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (sections 5.1-5.4, 6.1-6.4) plus repo landing page and README prose; 0 wet-lab steps (|W| = 0, all cohorts pre-existing), so computational coverage = 25/25 = 100%. Supplementary Methods S1.2-S1.6 and Supplementary Tables 1-3 are referenced by the Methods but were not fetched at stage 1.

Whether install.sh / pyproject.toml pin package sources, channels and the full direct-dependency set is unverified at stage 1.

gaps.missing: Processed GTEx and ADNI files cannot be shared under the data use agreements, so an independent assessor must regenerate every derived matrix from raw controlled-access data. This is legitimate controlled access (accessions resolve, DAC paths are documented) and is NOT penalized on the data axis, but it does mean the exact processed inputs to training are not obtainable as-is.
gaps.how_to_close: Where the DUA permits, deposit derived non-identifying artifacts (sample manifests, filtered gene lists, train/test donor split assignments) so the regeneration path is checkable even without the restricted matrices.
